title: A Simple "Experience Sampling" Method for Making Big Decisions About Your Career or Your Life our-career-or-your-life
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart presents experience sampling — a structured ten-day journaling practice — as a reliable tool for educators contemplating significant career or life changes. He opens by normalizing the mid-year restlessness that prompts such contemplations, using his own dual-career tension (classroom teacher and writer) as an illustration of the resource-constraint math many educators face. Stuart then reveals his personal productivity 'secret' as a corrective to mythologized notions of his output: he satisfices heavily in most areas to protect the domains where depth matters most. The experience sampling method itself is simple: set three phone alarms per day, and at each alarm jot a quick-response answer to three questions about which option you'd choose, a brief rationale, and your emotional state. After ten days, patterns in the data surface authentic preferences more reliably than a single moment of either impulsive or deliberate decision-making. Stuart notes the method has guided him back to the classroom multiple times and has been effective when taught to his high school daughter.
points: Experience sampling is a ten-day structured practice: three phone alarms per day, each prompting a brief notebook entry on which option you'd choose, a short rationale, and current emotional state.
Ten days of data reveals authentic preference patterns more reliably than a single moment of either impulsive or deliberate analysis.

Stuart's actual productivity strategy is heavy satisficing across most domains — stripping feedback to minimum viable, skipping social media, batch-producing blog content — to protect the few areas where depth compounds.
Mid-year career restlessness is predictable and nearly universal; naming it as a seasonal pattern rather than a crisis signal is itself a useful reframing.
Experience sampling works not only for major career decisions but as a teachable tool for high school students navigating significant personal choices.
quotes: I've got a feeling that more than a few of us have contemplated some degree of life or work change here in the 2025-26 school year. Whether it's a job or a role or a school or a city or a hobby or a haircut, change starts feeling tempting during these winter months.
My "secret" for somehow making it all work is that I'm remarkably average in most areas of my work. Basically, I satisfice the heck out of most things.
Were it not for the years-long pursuit of fluency in the work that matters most, my class would be a train wreck and my blog would be radio silence most weeks.
Whenever my ponderings get too serious, I'll sometimes use a tool called "experience sampling" to help me gain clarity.

For the next 10 days, set some alarms in your phone: one before school starts, one during lunch or on prep, one sometime after school is done. When the alarm goes off, grab your notebook and jot your first-response answers to a few questions

This method has reliably guided me in making the decision to stay in the classroom over the years and helped me gain clarity on why that's important to me. (One time I was even in consideration for the Director of Teaching and Learning position in my district, and this helped me confidently make the decision to bow out.)
